title: Prepare, open well, trade every step and listen
course_title: Negotiation Skills for Business and Life

say: Prepare, open well, trade every step, and listen.
This is the video for Module 2 of Negotiation Skills for Business and Life.
Twenty minutes of preparation with pen and paper will usually earn you more than an hour of clever talking.

panel.heading: A method you can repeat
items: Most deals are won before anyone speaks
Never give a concession for nothing
Questions reveal what they really need

say: In this module you learn why the first number has so much power, how to give ground without giving away your profit, and how listening reveals what the other side really needs.

panel.heading: A method you can repeat
items: Most deals are won before anyone speaks
Never give a concession for nothing
Questions reveal what they really need

say: Use one sheet for every important negotiation. Start with your goal in one sentence, why you want it, and what the other side might need.
Write your numbers. Your BATNA, walk-away point, target, and the opening offer you will make.
Collect evidence. Send the same short WhatsApp message to three suppliers, and write the lowest, highest and typical price. Prices move quickly, so this week's evidence beats last year's memory.
List tradeables. These are things you can give or ask for besides price: quantity, payment timing, delivery, packaging. The best ones are cheap for you but valuable to them.
Finally, write your opening line and three questions, and say them aloud twice.

panel.heading: Your preparation sheet
panel.rule: If any box is empty, you are not ready to start

say: Here is a worked example. Aisha's distributor says flour is going up from 68000 to 74000 naira a bag.

say: On 8 bags, that is 48000 more every week.

card.note: Agreed price. Approximate prices for illustration.

say: Two other distributors quote lower, but charge for delivery. So her BATNA is about 72625 a bag. Anything above that, and she should switch.

say: She opens at 70000, with tradeables ready. She can order 16 bags every two weeks, pay on delivery, or collect from the depot herself.

say: They settle at 71500 for fortnightly orders. That saves her 40000 over two weeks.

say: Psychologists call it anchoring. People are pulled toward the first number they hear. So when you have good information about market prices, go first.

panel.heading: The power of the first number
items: Go first when you know the market
Let them go first when you know little
Open ambitious, but with a reason
Extreme anchor? Name your own number

say: When you know very little, let them go first. Their number may be better than you expected.

say: Open above your target when selling, but close enough to explain. Say the number and its reason in the same breath.

say: If they open with an extreme number, do not move a little from it. Calmly say that is far from what the market shows, and name your own justified number.

say: Grace's walk-away is 430000 naira and her target is 470000. The client offers 400000. Grace does not jump. She asks what the budget is made up of.

card.title: Grace's catering package
card.note: Agreed: her target. Prices are approximate.

say: She had opened at 520000, including servers, cooler hire and clean-up.

card.title: Grace's catering package
card.note: Agreed: her target. Prices are approximate.

say: Now she trades rather than gives. If you provide your own drinks, I can do 490000.

card.title: Grace's catering package
card.note: Agreed: her target. Prices are approximate.

say: Then a smaller step. 475000 with small chops, if you pay a 60% deposit this week.

card.title: Grace's catering package
card.note: Agreed: her target. Prices are approximate.

say: They agree at 470000. Her steps shrank, 30000, then 15000, then 5000, which told the client the limit was near. And every step was traded for something.

card.title: Grace's catering package
card.note: Agreed: her target. Prices are approximate.

say: Use the if, then rule. If you can pay upfront, or take 20 pieces, then I can adjust the price. Every request has a cost.

panel.heading: Trade, do not give
left: If you pay upfront, then I can...

say: Avoid the common mistakes. Do not say my lowest is this. Do not split the difference when the middle is below your target. And never make two concessions in a row without getting anything back.

panel.heading: Trade, do not give

say: Now listening. Ifeoma sells beaded necklaces at 12000 naira each at a craft fair in Abuja. A buyer wants three and says the price is too high. Ifeoma mirrors. Too high?

cards.d: Repeat their last few important words as a gentle question: Too high?
Name the concern you notice: It sounds like you want to pay a fair price.
Restate their main points so they can confirm before you agree.

say: The buyer saw some for 7000 online. Ifeoma labels her worry, then explains. Those are usually plastic. These are glass beads with a metal clasp.

cards.d: Repeat their last few important words as a gentle question: Too high?
Name the concern you notice: It sounds like you want to pay a fair price.
Restate their main points so they can confirm before you agree.

say: She asks the budget, 30000, and offers a trade: 32000 for all three, with matching earrings for the bride.
The buyer pays by transfer, and Ifeoma checks the alert in her own bank app before handing over the goods.

cards.d: Repeat their last few important words as a gentle question: Too high?
Name the concern you notice: It sounds like you want to pay a fair price.
Restate their main points so they can confirm before you agree.

say: To remember. Prepare on one page with three current prices. Make concessions in shrinking steps, and trade every one.
Ask open questions that start with what or how. After you state your price, stop talking and count slowly to five.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Prepare on one page, every time
Trade every concession: if you, then I
Ask what and how, then stay silent
